full_sentence: Had the company invested in proper safety training, the accident would almost certainly have been avoided.

options.why_wrong: This is a general present statement and does not complete the past hypothetical set up by the inverted 'Had' clause.

options.text: the accident would happen again tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: The main clause must refer back to the past condition, so a present or future form does not fit this third conditional.

options.text: the accident would almost certainly have been avoided.

options.why_wrong: The main clause needs 'would have' plus a past participle to express the result of the unreal past condition; 'had been avoided' gives no conditional result.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional with 'Had' replacing 'If ... had'
explanation: In an inverted conditional, 'Had' plus subject and past participle replaces 'If ... had'. The main clause then uses 'would have' plus a past participle to describe the unreal past result. Polish speakers often reach for a simple conditional form here, but English requires 'would have' to match the past condition.
